title: Working and singing as a new man, and singing the blues
summary: Little singing at work; as a fresh fish he sang blues to himself, and sings a blues about drinking and women.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: Well, what about when you were working? Do they sing as much?
Well, they don't do as much singing when they're working, because it's mostly all working, not much singing.
When you first got here, what was it known?
Well, it wasn't quite as nice as it is now. We didn't have the building here that we got and we're sitting in right now. We had peas and corn planted here. The building wasn't here.
Did you work in the peas and corn?
I worked in the peas and corn, worked in plied, cut wood, pulled saws, worked in blacksmith shops, everywhere.

Well, most of the time when I'd be working, I'd listen to most of them sing myself. I didn't do too much singing because I was a new man here, so I guess I was what they call a fresh fish. I was a newly in there.
Any of the same songs that are on this record here?

Well, now those songs that was used by lots of them, but mostly by those that's who put that record out. They was mostly the ones that done that singing of that type. Most of the time when I sang, I'd mostly sang to myself and I'd mostly sang the blues then. I'd mostly sang that.
Tony, you don't remember the names of the songs that were singing here when you got here?

I believe I remember one or two, but not too many of those. Would you sing a little bit of those, too? I believe I might could if I tried a little bit. I sort of have a think I could. Alright. Some of them come a little fast, some of them come a little slow. I woke up this morning. I was feeling awful bad. One of them was the feeling that I ever had. Keep on drinking.
